:::{.proof}
We verify symmetry and idempotency.
Both use that $\tp{\mX}\mX$ is symmetric,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tp{\paren{\tp{\mX}\mX}} &= \tp{\mX}\,\tp{\paren{\tp{\mX}}} \\
&= \tp{\mX}\mX
\end{aligned}
$$

(@thm-transpose-product),
so its inverse is symmetric too (@cor-inverse-symmetric).

**Symmetry:**
$$\ba
\tp{\matr{H}}
&= \tp{\left(\mX(\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\tp{\mX}\right)}
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{H} \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{(\tp{\mX})} \cdot \tp{\left((\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\right)} \cdot \tp{\mX}
&& \text{(transpose of a product, twice)}
\\
&= \mX \cdot \tp{\left((\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\right)} \cdot \tp{\mX}
&& \text{(transposing twice changes nothing)}
\\
&= \mX \cdot (\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1} \cdot \tp{\mX}
&& \text{(the inverse of a symmetric matrix is symmetric)}
\\
&= \matr{H}
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{H} \text{)}
\ea$$

**Idempotency:**
$$\ba
\matr{H}^2
&= \mX(\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\tp{\mX} \cdot \mX(\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\tp{\mX}
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{H} \text{)}
\\
&= \mX(\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}(\tp{\mX}\mX)(\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\tp{\mX}
&& \text{(regroup; matrix multiplication is associative)}
\\
&= \mX\,\matr{I}_p\,(\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\tp{\mX}
&& \text{(definition of the inverse)}
\\
&= \mX(\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1}\tp{\mX}
&& \text{(identity matrix)}
\\
&= \matr{H}
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{H} \text{)}
\ea$$
:::
